content:
Maya: heads up — after last routing tweak some SSE clients hit 429s way earlier than expected. console shows backpressure spike but quota meters look fine.

Sasha: saw a few alerts, thought it was transient. do you have tenant examples?

Maya: tenant=alpha-prod, around 10:12 UTC. attaching a small log snippet.

Maya: ```
2026-03-21T10:12:03Z proxy=B pool=B instance=proxy-7 sse_conn_open tenant=alpha-prod
2026-03-21T10:12:07Z proxy=B pool=B instance=proxy-7 sse_429 tenant=alpha-prod reason=backpressure_holdoff
2026-03-21T10:12:10Z proxy=B pool=B instance=proxy-7 sse_conn_close tenant=alpha-prod
```

Ben: thanks — that `backpressure_holdoff` reason is the proxy applying the route-level holdoff. the odd part is console shows SSE backpressure for a different tenant group (alpha-staging). mapping bug?

Lee: console code maps the telemetry label `tenant_group` -> UI bucket via the `ui-bucket` map. i remember a PR that added fallback logic for empty tenant_group, maybe it collides with the new routing-affinity label `route_shard`.

Sasha: evidence: aggregator is sending `sse_backpressure{tenant_group="",route_shard="B"}` -> console bucket resolves to default -> shows on alpha-staging because staging is the default. so it's a label collapse.

KM: i'm checking the metric ingestion path. quick prometheus-ish query to prove it: 

KM: ```
sum by (tenant_group,route_shard)(rate(sse_backpressure_total[1m]))
```

KM: results show high rate for `tenant_group=""` and `route_shard="B"`. no tenant_group tag = collapse.

Maya: ok that explains the mismatch between backpressure UI and actual tenant 429s. what are options? patch aggregator to preserve `tenant_id` label or make console group by `tenant_id` first?

Lee: i prefer changing the aggregator to never drop tenant labels. console grouping change is riskier for existing dashboards. patch path: aggregator change -> small config bump -> canary.

Ben: +1 aggregator. also we should not rely on empty-string fallback mapping in UI. we can add a UI-level annotation to show when `tenant_group==""` so it's obvious.

Sasha: quick mitigation: relax proxy holdoff policy for pool B so alpha-prod recovers while we patch telemetry. change `holdoff_ms` from 1200 -> 300 for pool B. small risk to overload but reduces 429 churn.

Maya: propose rollout plan:
1) patch aggregator to forward `tenant_id` label (PR 1)
2) deploy aggregator patch to canary (10% traffic, pool B only)
3) revert proxy holdoff to safe default after canary verifies
4) UI annotation + dashboard panel for `tenant_group==""`

Lee: for canary we can use feature flag `sse_label_preserve_v2` via rollout service. console will show tagged traces once v2 is on.

Sasha: i'll open PRs. can we also add an eval metric: `sse_429_per_tenant` and alert if > 5/min sustained for 5m?

KM: i'll add an ad-hoc dashboard and the alert rule. query: `sum by (tenant_id)(rate(sse_429_total[5m]))` threshold 0.083 (5/min).

Ben: also we should track socket-churn: `sum by (proxy_pool)(rate(sse_conn_open[1m])) / avg by (proxy_pool)(sse_active_connections)` to detect pain early.

Maya: timeline: PRs today, canary in staging tonight, 10% prod canary tomorrow morning. Sasha + KM to run canary and post checks.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: feature=sse_label_preserve_v2 scope=pool-B percent=10

Sasha: canary started. i'm watching metrics. initial 10m looks clean, alpha-prod 429s dropped to 0 in the sample window.

Lee: will push UI annotation change in a separate patch (non-blocking).

Maya: nice. after canary we revert the proxy holdoff tweak and roll the aggregator everywhere. also add a note in the rollout UX doc about how console groups empty labels.

KM: created dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/board/sse-backpressure-canary with the new panels and alerts.

Ben: remind ops to mute noisy alerts during the canary window and re-enable after verification.

Maya: thanks team — good catch on the empty-label collapse. follow-up: action items in #eng-platform tickets.

Sasha: filing PRs now.

Maya: ping me when PRs are green and we can schedule the widening rollout. :thumbsup:
